name: XDKNet 2.6.0
body:
Android TV 2.6.0. No server plugin update is needed: XDKNet plugin
2.1.0.16 (Emby 2.0.5.16) stays current.

TVs on 2.4.10 or later offer this update on their own. On 2.4.9, use
Settings > About > Check for updates. Anything older has to install it once
by hand, from the `XDKNet_AndroidTV.apk` below.

A large release: features and fixes brought over from Moonfin 2.7 to 3.1.
Nothing changes how the app looks until you choose it, apart from Who's
watching and Switch User.

## Three new details screen styles

Under Settings > Personalization > Details Screen > Details Screen Style,
beside Classic and Modern. Modern stays the style until you pick another.

- **Stage** leads with the poster, down the left of the screen with Play and
  the other buttons under it. The title, ratings, overview, the people
  behind a film, a show's seasons or a season's episodes sit beside it, and
  the cast, extras, collections and More Like This run underneath.
- **Premiere** centres the title over a backdrop that fills the first
  screen, with the buttons and ratings under it. Everything else is one
  press of Down away, section by section.
- **Quick Look** opens a title in a drawer down the right of the screen,
  over the screen it was picked on: its name and numbers, the buttons, the
  overview and a show's seasons. Open full page goes to the full screen, and
  Back closes the drawer.

## Time's up

- When a Jellyfin admin has given a user the hours they may use the server,
  the app now stops at the end of those hours: what is playing stops and a
  Time's up screen says when they can come back, with Switch User on it.
  Before, a film carried on until it began to fail, with nothing to say why.
- The screen lifts by itself when the hours open again, and a change the
  admin makes is picked up within a minute. Administrators are not held to a
  schedule.

## The player

Under Settings > Playback & SyncPlay > Video Playback Preferences.

- **Hide Controls After** sets how long the controls stay up after the last
  press: 1, 3 or 5 seconds.
- **Dim Controls in HDR** dims the controls over an HDR picture, where plain
  white is far brighter than the film.
- Playback speed goes up to 5x.
- The chapter picker is a row of chapter cards with their pictures, not a
  list of names.
- A subtitle the server has to prepare first says "Fetching subtitles" while
  it is on its way, instead of showing nothing.
- **Let TV Sleep After**, in the screensaver settings, closes XDKNet after
  15, 30, 60 or 120 minutes without a button press, so the TV's own
  screensaver and sleep timer can take over. Anything paused keeps its
  place. It is off until turned on, and never closes the app while
  something is playing.

## Home

- **Hide Watched** for the Recently Added and Recently Released rows, in
  the Home rows settings. It starts as your account has it on the server,
  which for most accounts is on, so Recently Released may now leave out what
  you have watched. Turn it off there to see everything again.
- **Hide Unwatched Count** takes the number of episodes left off the
  posters, under Settings > Personalization > Home Screen, beside Hide Watch
  Progress.
- Each library's Latest row and each pinned collection row ends with a See
  All card that opens the library or the collection.
- **Show Calendar Button**, under Settings > Personalization > Navigation,
  puts the Calendar in the side menu. It is off until turned on.
- **Date Format**, under Settings > Personalization > General Style, shows
  dates in the Calendar, the Upcoming rows and air dates as month then day,
  day then month, or the way your language does.
- **UI Scale** has two larger steps, Grandparents and Great-Grandparents,
  for reading the app from further away.

## Libraries and playlists

- **Library Order**, under Settings > Personalization > Libraries, moves
  your libraries with Left and Right. My Media, the recently added rows and
  the side menu follow it, and so do your other apps, since the order is
  saved to your account on the server.
- Holding OK on a title inside a playlist or a collection offers Remove from
  Playlist or Remove from Collection.
- A playlist's items have View Details, after Play and Play Next. Back
  returns to the playlist. With the Classic details style, OK on a film in a
  playlist now plays it, as Modern already did.

## Search

- Results show after about a second even when the server is slow to search
  for people. People fills in when it arrives, without moving what you have
  selected.
- A row is no longer left empty because hundreds of episodes or songs
  matched first: playlists, collections and videos that the first page left
  out are searched for on their own.
- Channels are found without typing their accents.

## Links from outside the app

- XDKNet now opens `xdknet://` links, so a launcher or a remote-button
  mapper can go straight to a place in the app: `xdknet://home`,
  `xdknet://search?query=...`, `xdknet://live-tv/guide`,
  `xdknet://live-tv/recordings`, and `xdknet://item?id=...` or
  `xdknet://play?id=...` for a title.
- Adding `userId=...` to a home, item or play link opens it as that user
  when they are signed in on the TV. It never gets past a PIN.

## Live TV

- The player's controls have a heart beside Channels that makes the channel
  you are watching a favourite, or stops it being one. The guide follows.
- Stop on the remote leaves the channel and returns to the guide, also with
  the in-player guide or channel list open.
- Play and Pause on the remote work on a live channel.
- Cancelling a recording from Schedule works. It failed for every recording
  the server listed with its programme, which is nearly all of them.
- Scheduled recordings are grouped by your own day, so one in the evening no
  longer shows under Tomorrow, and Today and Tomorrow stay right across a
  clock change.

## Who's watching and Switch User

- Both screens have a new look. The account you are on sits large in the
  middle with the others fading out either side; Left and Right move between
  them and OK picks one. On a wide TV more of them show at once.
- Under each name the screen says what picking it takes: already signed in
  on this TV, a password, or the PIN set for it on this TV, which also puts a
  lock on the picture. Someone without a profile picture gets their initial on
  a colour of their own.
- Who's watching says "Signing in..." while it signs you in, which on the
  first sign-in to a server can take a few seconds. Pressing OK again while it
  does no longer starts the sign-in over.
- In Switch User, OK on your own picture still opens the profile picture
  screen, and the picture carries a camera badge to say so. Add User, Select
  Server, Profile Picture, the year in review and Sign Out are a row of
  buttons along the bottom.
- Forgot PIN works: signing in with the account's password after it clears
  the PIN, instead of asking for the PIN again.
- Back on Who's watching and on the sign-in screen goes back a screen instead
  of offering to close the app. A server with no users to show no longer
  bounces between the sign-in screen and an empty list.

## Playback fixes

- Skipping the credits of a film or of a show's last episode no longer closes
  the player when there is a scene after them. It closes only when the
  credits run to the end.
- The next episode keeps the subtitle track you picked. Before, a "forced"
  track in the same language, listed first in the file, could take its place
  and show only the signs.
- Dolby Digital Plus above 5.1 (most Atmos from streaming services) that the
  server sends as a converted stream no longer restarts the TV's audio
  decoder on every frame.
- A file whose container the TV's player cannot read, such as an AVI with an
  odd-sized chunk, now plays converted by the server instead of failing.
- A file that marks every audio track as the default no longer starts on the
  first track whatever its language. With none of your languages in it, it
  starts in English if it has it.
- With the mpv player, an episode whose tracks are laid out differently from
  the last one keeps your audio and subtitle choice.

## Getting around

- A screen opens with its first item selected, not its last.
- Back closes Settings the second time it is opened too, on TVs with
  Android 14.
- After backing out of a screen opened from the side menu, the first press of
  Left opens the menu again.
- Seerr's Requests and Issues no longer pop the side menu open while they
  load.
- When voice search can't start, the remote is no longer left with nothing
  selected.
- A text field's placeholder hides while the keyboard is open, so it no longer
  reads as text already typed.

## Seerr and lists

- A season pack counts once towards a request's download progress, not once
  per episode.
- Custom list rows wait longer for a long list before giving up, and adding
  or editing one says what actually went wrong.
- The copy of a custom list row kept on the TV now belongs to the account
  that loaded it. Before, the next account on the same TV could be shown a
  row loaded under another one, whatever its own parental limit, until the
  row refreshed.

## Emby

- Group Items into Collections hides the films that are in a collection.
- A library no longer shows up twice.
- Creating and renaming playlists works again.

## Also

- New playlists on Jellyfin are private, as they are in Jellyfin's own apps.
- A server behind a proxy that relabels its ping reply is no longer taken for
  unreachable, which left Home empty.
- A media bar trailer from YouTube stays inside its box on Fire TV.
- A download converted by the server keeps the film's embedded picture
  subtitles (PGS).
